summary.one_liner: A deliberately minimal JavaScript compiler that walks through the major stages of a modern compiler (tokenizing, parsing, transforming, code generation) in a small, readable codebase.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes this as an ultra-simplified example of all the major pieces of a modern compiler, written in easy-to-read JavaScript. The main code lives in the-super-tiny-compiler.js, which the README points to as the place to start reading. The README says reading the guided code should teach how most compilers work from end to end. A test suite is provided and run with `node test.js`. The README does not list specific language features or output formats beyond this.
use_cases: learning how compilers work end to end
studying a small compiler implementation in JavaScript
reference for building a toy language compiler
how_to_run: Run the tests with: node test.js
notable: Written as a tiny, heavily guided codebase meant to be read top to bottom
Covers the major pieces of a modern compiler in one file
Listed in codecrafters-io/build-your-own-x under 'Build your own Programming Language'
caveats: The README does not describe the input or output language or supported syntax
The README does not state a license
Educational example, not a production compiler
